m:ayasofya: Foreign visitors pay €25 to go up to the upper gallery, while the ground floor is a place of worship (price from secondary sources and official resellers, to be confirmed on the Ministry of Culture website, muze.gen.tr). Hours given by sources: every day about 9am–7pm, last entry around 6:30pm, but tourists can't enter during the five prayers and on Fridays at midday the break is long (about noon–2:30pm). Shoulders and knees covered, women with a scarf over their hair (available at the entrance), shoes off. Sources disagree on whether the Museum Pass covers the gallery: check before buying it. Queues are shorter at opening and in the last hour.
m:sultanahmet: Entry to the mosque is free, but it's closed to tourists during the five daily prayers (and for a long time on Fridays at midday): arrive with a free hour ahead of you. Covered clothing is required, women must cover their hair (scarves lent at the entrance) and shoes come off. In recent years the mosque has been restored in phases and parts of the interior may be covered by scaffolding: I couldn't check the state of the works in October 2026. The Hippodrome is an open square, accessible all day.
m:topkapi: Closed every Tuesday. Sources give the ticket office as open every day from 9am to 5pm or until 6:30pm on summer hours (until 31 October): on winter hours plan to finish by 5pm. The combined ticket for foreigners, covering the palace, Harem and Hagia Irene, is about 2,750 TL (about €50–55); the lira price changes fast, check it on muze.gen.tr. The Harem is paid separately and isn't included in the Museum Pass (one source says it is: to be confirmed). Allow at least three hours and go at opening time.
m:cisterna: Open every day, usually about 9am to 6pm (hours from guides, to be confirmed on the official website). The ticket for foreigners is between about 1,300 TL and €38 depending on the source (not included in the Museum Pass): check the price, which changes often in lira. You walk on wooden walkways, with a damp floor and dim light. Queues are longest mid-morning: better to book online.
m:archeo: Price for foreigners about €15–17 (650 TL according to an April 2026 source, to be confirmed). Usually 9am–6pm with last entry an hour earlier, closed on Mondays (from guides, not read on the official website). The ticket is included in the Museum Pass Istanbul.
m:bazar: Open Monday to Saturday, usually from 9am to 7pm (sources give opening times between 8:30 and 10am); closed on Sundays and on the first day of religious holidays. Entry is free. Haggling is normal: start at about half the price they ask. Beware of people who stop you in the street and invite you into a shop, and of pickpockets in the crowd. No price is fixed: compare several shops before buying.
m:suleymaniye: Entry is free, but the mosque is closed to tourists during the five daily prayers and covered clothing applies, with a scarf for women (source not checked on the official website: check Istanbul's prayer times on the day). The gardens and the cemetery with Sinan's tomb are open all day.
m:spezie: Open every day, usually about 8am to 7:30pm (hours from guides, to be confirmed). Entry is free. Prices aren't always displayed: ask and taste before buying, and compare several stalls. In the most touristy shops prices are higher than in the surrounding streets.
m:galata: Price for foreigners about €30 (sources give about 1,750 TL, April 2026 data, to be confirmed). Hours: sources disagree, giving every day from 8:30 or 9am to 7pm or 11pm; plan to arrive before 7pm. There's a lift. A 2023 source reported the outdoor terrace being restored: I couldn't check this. The Museum Pass covers the tower. At sunset the queue is long: book online.
m:istiklal: Free to walk at any hour, and very lively in the evening. The T2 heritage tram runs from Tünel to Taksim (with the Istanbulkart). It's an area where pickpockets are active: keep your bag and phone in front of you. During demonstrations Taksim square and the surrounding streets may be closed by the police.
m:bosforo: Üsküdar takes about 15 minutes, Kadıköy about 25. The fare is about 45–55 TL per trip with the Istanbulkart (about €1; fares from an early-2026 list, probably higher after the 20 July increase: to be confirmed). Times and prices on sehirhatlari.istanbul. There's also the long Bosphorus tour on a public ferry or with private operators, whose times and prices I didn't check.
m:kadikoy: The market is open every day (some stalls close on Sunday evening). Take the ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy, 20–25 minutes. It's much quieter and more authentic than the historic centre, with lower prices for meals.
vd:pudding: A historic Sultanahmet spot, open since 1957, a meeting point for travellers on the «hippie trail» to the East. Turkish breakfasts with olives, cheeses, eggs and bread, and simple hot dishes, a short walk from the tram.
vp:pudding: A Turkish breakfast costs about €8–12, a dish with a drink about €8–14 (menu not seen, prices in lira that change fast). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:kofteci: A historic meatball restaurant in Sultanahmet, open since 1920: order a plate of grilled köfte with bean salad and a piece of bread, and eat in a simple room. The classic lunch a few steps from Hagia Sophia.
vp:kofteci: A plate of köfte with salad costs about €8–12 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:hocapasa: A pidecisi, a pide place: the elongated, boat-shaped Turkish pizza baked in a wood-fired oven, with meat, cheese, eggs or spinach. A small room near Sirkeci station, also popular with locals.
vp:hocapasa: A pide with a drink costs about €7–11 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:kurukahve: The historic Turkish coffee shop, open since 1871 at the foot of the Spice Bazaar: buy ground coffee, get a cup to go and watch people go by. There's almost always a queue, and it's quick.
vp:kurukahve: A coffee to go costs about €1.50–3, a 100-gram pack about €3–5 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:balik: Istanbul's most famous fish sandwich: a grilled mackerel fillet in a bun with onion and salad, sold on the quay near the Galata Bridge. Eaten standing or on stools, in front of the ferries.
vp:balik: A sandwich costs about €4–7 (price not read, in lira). Hours and stalls vary from day to day: to be confirmed.
vd:gullu: The city's best-known baklava shop, run by the Güllüoğlu family since 1949 in Karaköy: pistachio and walnut baklava, börek and sütlaç, a baked rice pudding. Eat at the counter or at little tables.
vp:gullu: A portion of baklava costs about €4–8, a börek with tea about €4–7 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:karakoy: A lokanta, the modern Turkish canteen, in a former bank building: cold mezze, fish, meat dishes and seasonal vegetables. A smart setting but neighbourhood-canteen prices.
vp:karakoy: A dish with a mezze costs about €12–20 (menu not seen, in lira). Best to book in the evening. Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:mandabatmaz: A small bar in a side passage off İstiklal, known for its thick, foamy Turkish coffee. Low tables and stools, very popular with young people.
vp:mandabatmaz: A Turkish coffee costs about €1.50–3 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:zubeyir: An ocakbaşı, a place with the grill in the middle of the room: sit around the fire and order lamb or chicken skewers, liver, grilled vegetables and salads. A noisy atmosphere and generous plates, good for dinner.
vp:zubeyir: A dinner with skewers and a salad costs about €15–25 per person (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:van: Eastern Anatolian breakfast in Cihangir: cheese, olives, honey with kaymak (clotted cream), eggs with sucuk (spicy sausage), warm bread and tea from the samovar. Shared at the table; there are queues at weekends.
vp:van: Breakfast for two costs about €15–25 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:ciya: A Kadıköy restaurant famous for regional Anatolian dishes: soups, stuffed vegetables, skewers, stews and desserts that change every day. Choose by looking at the dishes on display, which you can taste before ordering.
vp:ciya: A meal with several tastes costs about €12–20 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
vd:baylan: A 1923 Kadıköy pâtisserie with marble tables and cake displays: the speciality is «kup griye», ice cream with custard and nuts. Also breakfast with simit (sesame bread ring) and tea.
vp:baylan: Breakfast costs about €5–9, a kup griye about €4–7 (menu not seen, in lira). Hours from guides, to be confirmed.
cd:dolmabahce: The Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus, with the throne room and crystal chandeliers.
cx:dolmabahce: Closed Monday and Thursday. The price depends on the route chosen (Selamlık, Harem).
cn:turcoislamico: Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts
cd:turcoislamico: Carpets, manuscripts and ceramics in Ibrahim Pasha's palace, opposite the Hippodrome.
cd:hamam: A 1741 Turkish bath, with massage and scrub.
cx:hamam: The price depends on the package chosen.
cd:rumeli: The fortress on the Bosphorus built by Mehmed II before the conquest of Constantinople.
cx:rumeli: It's about 12 km north of the centre.
cd:modern: Turkish modern and contemporary art, in a Renzo Piano building on the Bosphorus.
cd:pera: Orientalism and Anatolian textiles in a Beyoğlu palace.
cd:maiden: A tower on an islet in the Bosphorus, with a restaurant and views of the city.
cx:maiden: Reached by boat from Üsküdar or Salacak.
cd:rahmi: Transport and industry, with a submarine and a locomotive on the Golden Horn.
